{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegan_cuisine|Vegan Cuisine]]

Every vegan should know about aioli and related sauces. They add a creaminess which can be otherwise rare in vegan cooking. The key to the not-vegan-tasting deliciousness of an aioli is the garlic/olive oil emulsion. The same principle is at work in hummus (or marinara). Other common emulsifiers are glycerin, soy [[Cookbook:Lecithin|lecithin]] (present in [[Cookbook:Soy Milk|soymilk]], [[Cookbook:Tofu|tofu]], etc.) and [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolk]].

==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 5 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|serrano chile]]
* 100–200 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]] juice (any other citrus works)
* French-style or [[Cookbook:Dijon Mustard|Dijon mustard]] (i.e. one that does not contain "turmeric" in the list of ingredients; optional)
==Procedure==
# Cut carrots extremely fine (i.e. 1 [[Cookbook:Mm|mm]] slivers) so that blender can handle it.
# Combine all ingredients. Use a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] to start blending everything together.
# Continue blending in additional olive oil until it reaches desired creaminess.
# Adjust seasoning to taste.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Carrots can damage some blending equipment. It is recommended to cut them into really small pieces so they're easier to blend.

==See also==
* [[Cookbook:Creamy Aioli Salsa|Creamy Aioli Salsa]]
